I play a lot of spy. If any of you have questions about the class, I can answer them at a semi-competent level!
Do you have any tips for shitty spies like me?

Well, to a certain extent, the first thing anyone who's played tf2 for a while will think of when someone asks for nonspecific advice to improve is to practice. I have to say that first, because giving advice without saying that practice is important is just completely illegitimate. After that, though, I should make something clear: spy is one of the least "mechanically-focused" classes in the game, meaning that raw skills like aiming and fancy button-pressing are less important for spy than they are for almost any other class in the game, just because of the way that you secure most of your kills. tf2 is a twitch shooter, though, so those mechanics are still very important, it's just not the end-all, be-all that it is with other classes like Sniper.

The easiest way to get better with spy is to start actively thinking about what each other person in the game wants to be doing. This means having a familiarity with every class, every game mode, and every map, within reason. That way, when you get into a game, you can think to yourself "where does X or Y player on the enemy team want to go, and what does he want to do once he's there?" and have that be at least a semi-accurate prediction. You basically get two things from doing that: one, you'll be able to predict the approximate front lines in a linear map, allowing you to more effectively get behind the majority of useful enemy players at once, and two, you'll be able to more accurately predict individual enemy player's movements, making you much more effective at stalking and eliminating classes that are the same speed or even faster than you.

I guess as a general tip, too, try to play in a way that's fun for you, because first off, you won't improve as spy if you're hating every moment of your time that you spend as spy, and second, fun is really the end goal 99% of the time anyway, so make sure to keep fun in mind, and take a break or play as another class if you're getting annoyed.
What's the best map to practice spy on?

To be honest, you shouldn't be thinking about "maps to spy on." You can and should play spy everywhere, especially considering that the better you know a map, the better you'll be with spy on that map.

If you're just asking about the most fun kinds of maps to play on, though, to get into a rhythm or something, then I would suggest playing some KOTH. It's generally more fast-paced than other game modes in pubs, and it works very well with (occasionally recklessly) aggressive play, which is something I personally enjoy.

Out of the stock maps, I would only suggest actively avoiding Dustbowl and 2fort (and maybe Junction, too.) They're both terribly designed, overly chokey maps, and that makes it pretty fucking annoying to play spy (or any class, honestly) on them a lot of the time.
Is it better to run to the enemy side cloaked or disguised? And what's the best way to get around unnoticed/blend in?

My sincere apologies for the late reply, I've spent the last several days crying myself to sleep over the DR nerf, and as such, have not been able to see my screen through the tears.

Joking aside, the answer to this question just got a lot more one-dimensional since the ludicrous nerf to the only fun pub watch.

If you have the option, cloaked is always, always better. With the new DR, I would even consider trying to get ticked by a hitscan weapon from long range, just so you can cloak across the line. It's the difference between people being able to see through a disguise and shoot you, which isn't hard, and not being able to see you at all. I think you can see the advantages of being invisible.

As for the best way to get around unnoticed or blend in, there are several ways to do so. The first, and best, is to be where people aren't. This just requires a general feel of the flow of the battlefield along with a decent level of map knowledge. This clearly isn't always possible, though, so you have to move to the second best method: don't let them see you. This, most obviously, can be achieved by being behind them, but frequently, being above or below them works as well. Of course, you're probably going to have to get into position to get things done a lot of the time while you can't be totally unseen, so you have to move to the third, and likely least effective method: acting. This constitutes being disguised as a class, and acting to the enemy team like you actually are that class. In addition to being one of the least effective ways to not get shot at as a spy, it's also one of the most difficult to get down properly, so a lot of people don't bother with it at all. That's too bad, though, because at higher levels, it's basically the only chance you have of anyone buying any disguise, so it's important to practice it sometimes. Like I mentioned in another post here, an important thing for spies to have in mind is what they think their opponents want to be doing. In addition to being useful for predicting the enemy team's movements and where people that you can't see might be, it can also help to make a disguise believable, by acting like someone on the enemy team would be acting if they were the class you were disguised as in the place you were at the time.

Stabby, love him or hate him, makes some pretty educational videos, and he talks a little bit about acting in some of them. Because acting basically encompasses knowledge of every class in the game, it can be a little difficult to write general tips about, but seeing video demonstrating concepts while someone is talking about them can be pretty helpful.

I found one spot in a video where he talks specifically about acting for a clip. It's short, but it's a pretty effective demonstration of acting:

Time is in the link, but for mobile users, it's at 2:57.

well whenever I get by lag, I get hit by spies the worst. I just notice how frequently spy and sniper are the most picked classes and spy more consistently makes it to the top of the scoreboard. What do you do against someone like that?

That's actually a pretty good question. With too much lag, it'll be quite difficult to do anything against a decent spy, but at that point, it'll also be pretty much impossible to do well against anyone else.

There's two things you mentioned here, though, that I think I can specifically address. What spies do to "choose" when people see them, as you know, is one or both of two things. Cloaking, for one, or disguising. Each of these can be countered individually.

Disguises can be a bit annoying to get used to seeing through, but with a little practice (and especially practicing as spy yourself) it'll get a lot easier. There are some specific things you can watch out for, though.

First, and most obviously, you can look at the movement of the players around you. I'm not really talking about looking for slow scouts, although that works too. Watch for suspicious movement. Is the other player moving in a way that won't take them towards your team's objective? If so, is he moving like an inexperienced player would? If not, is he moving towards you, your teammates, or a sentry nest, especially their respective backs? That can be a clear giveaway of a spy a surprising amount of the time.

Second, try to see what your teammates (or disguised spies) want to do most of the time. This ties in with movement to a degree, and can be a little vague, but based on how everyone's facing around you and where they appear to be going, you should be able to get an alright idea of what they'll be doing in the next few seconds. Is there anyone that looks like they don't have a clear objective, or that looks like their objective is to surreptitiously get behind you and your teammates? That could be an indicator of a disguised spy as well.

Third, and this can sometimes be even more vague, but you can pay even closer attention to the facing of the players around you. As a spy, it can be difficult at times to keep from scanning the enemies around me for information like health, positioning, and even how competent they look. If anyone looks to be scanning your team for information, that can also be a way you can tell who a spy is.

This is fairly mid-level advice on disguising and basic acting, and it also assumes you know some basics like how to watch for players who are avoiding walking through you at all costs. It has counters, and more sophisticated acting along the lines of backpedaling and controlling who you're facing can add another layer of obfuscation. However, it's a good start, and you'll get a better instinct for spies as time goes on.

After disguises, though, you have to think about cloaking. Other classes all have their movement options to get around the battlefield, from the heavy's GRU to soldier's rocket jumping, and the spy's movement enabler is his cloak. What that means is that the spy's cloak, like the other movement enhancers that I mentioned the other classes have, is not an offensive tool. a spy's chief offensive tool, and this is true for the other classes too, is positioning. A watch might get you behind your enemy, but that's only a means to an end, and the end is having superior positioning. So, and this ties pretty heavily into the next part that I'm writing, you have to ask yourself: "Where does a cloaked spy want to go right now?" From there, there's a pretty good chance that you'll be able to get a slightly better idea of where those invisible assholes are.

Something that can help a lot beyond that is memorizing ammo locations on the map. If a spy cloaks or dead rings around you, where does their most effective escape route take them, and where might they go to feel the most comfortable with the amount of cloak time that they have? A lot of times, this is going to take them through ammo pickups. You can chase cloaked spies with relative ease with many of the classes if you internalize this information, and even if you don't ultimately kill them, you've still denied them their goal, and ultimately reduced their effectiveness. And, even better, if YOU are their goal, having the ability to fight back against them will make their jobs that much harder.

For my final point on watches (for now,) remember that if a spy on the enemy team is using dead ringer, that makes it impossible for them to cloak on demand, and will affect their behavior when cloaked. I might write some more about that later, but this is already quite a long post.

The second thing you said that caught me, though, was about prediction. That's a bit of a trickier subject, but a basic rundown goes a little like this. (I'll try to keep it short.)

Prediction isn't actually about figuring out what your enemies are going to do. It's about figuring out what they WANT to do. You can kind of extend my second point about watching your own team to the enemy team too. What is their goal? I don't just mean the biggest thing, (oh gosh, what game mode am I playing?) but what steps they might take towards that goal. If there's a problematic sentry nest on your team, or your players are able to sit back and build uber or something, you can be pretty sure that the goal of any competent players on the opposing team is going to be to counter your play. A spy's ultimate goal on a life might be to take out that nest, or somehow disrupt your combo. With this information, you can figure out pretty much where the spy might go, both when you can and when you cannot see him. (Playing spy yourself helps immensely with this part, too.) With that in mind, you'll be able to chase cloaked spies much more effectively, and probably end up getting better at spy yourself. Spy is heavily about movement, from the tricks to the disguises to the watches, so getting used to how a competent spy moves will help you in both emulating them, and finding them when you're not playing spy yourself (or even when you are, realistically.)
